Parameters module

Parameter management for the GUMP GPD fitting framework.

This module converts the flat 1-D parameter arrays expected by minimizers (e.g. iMinuit) into the structured multi-dimensional arrays consumed by the conformal-moment calculation routines.

Parameter array layout

Each GPD species is parameterized per flavor as a set of ansatz terms. A single ansatz term contains six numbers:

[norm, alpha, beta, alphap, bexp, invm2]

The structured output of ParaManager_Unp() and ParaManager_Pol() has shape (2, 3, 5, n_ansatz, 6) where the axes correspond to:

  • axis 0 – GPD pair: [H, E] or [\~H, \~E]

  • axis 1 – skewness power: [xi^0, xi^2, xi^4] terms

  • axis 2 – flavor: [u_V, u-bar, d_V, d-bar, g]

  • axis 3 – ansatz index

  • axis 4 – parameter within one ansatz: [norm, alpha, beta, alphap, bexp, invm2]

gumpgpd.Parameters.ConfMoment(j: complex, t: float, ParaSets: ndarray) → complex[source]

Evaluate the conformal (Mellin) moment \(F(j, t)\) for a single ansatz.

The ansatz follows the Kumerički–Müller (KM) form:

\[F(j, t) = \frac{N}{B(2-\alpha, 1+\beta)}\, B(j+1-\alpha-\alpha^\prime t,\,1+\beta)\, e^{b_{\text{exp}}\,t}\, (1 - t / m^2)^{-2}\]

where \(B\) is the Euler Beta function (see beta_loggamma()).

Parameters:

  • j (complex) – conformal spin variable (the physical conformal spin is \(j+2\), but the offset is absorbed into the normalization).

  • t (float) – momentum transfer squared.

  • ParaSets (np.ndarray) –

    parameter array with last dimension of size 6, laid out as [norm, alpha, beta, alphap, bexp, invm2]:

    • norm – overall normalization \(N\)

    • alpha – small-\(x\) Regge intercept

    • beta – large-\(x\) power

    • alphap – Regge slope \(\alpha^\prime\)

    • bexp – exponential \(t\)-slope

    • invm2 – inverse mass squared \(1/m^2\) for the dipole residual; set to 0 to disable

Returns:

conformal moment \(F(j, t)\) with the same leading shape as ParaSets[..., 0].

Return type:

complex or np.ndarray

Note

ParaSets may carry arbitrary leading dimensions. The typical usage is:

  • j shape (N,), t shape (), ParaSets shape (5, n_ansatz, 6) – used when integrating over \(j\).

  • j shape (N,), t shape (N,), ParaSets shape (N, 5, n_ansatz, 6) – vectorized over kinematics.

The function reshapes j and t to broadcast correctly with the leading dimensions of ParaSets.

gumpgpd.Parameters.Moment_Sum(j: complex, t: float, ParaSets: ndarray) → complex[source]

Sum conformal moments over all ansatz terms.

When ParaSets contains multiple ansatz terms (e.g. a valence term plus a sea term), ConfMoment() returns one contribution per term along the last axis. This function reduces that axis by summing, yielding the total conformal moment for each flavor.

Parameters:

  • j (complex) – conformal spin variable; see ConfMoment().

  • t (float) – momentum transfer squared.

  • ParaSets (np.ndarray) – parameter array whose last axis has length 6 and whose second-to-last axis indexes the ansatz terms; shape (..., 5, n_ansatz, 6).

Returns:

sum of conformal moments over all ansatz terms; shape (..., 5).

Return type:

complex or np.ndarray

gumpgpd.Parameters.ParaManager_Pol(Paralst: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Convert a flat polarized parameter list into a structured array.

Analogous to ParaManager_Unp() but for the helicity GPDs ~H (Ht) and ~E (Et).

The output has shape (2, 3, 5, n_ansatz, 6) whose axes are:

  • axis 0 – GPD: [~H, ~E]

  • axis 1 – skewness power: [xi^0, xi^2, xi^4]

  • axis 2 – flavor: [u_V, u-bar, d_V, d-bar, g]

  • axis 3 – ansatz index

  • axis 4 – parameters per ansatz: [norm, alpha, beta, alphap, bexp, invm2]

Parameters:

Paralst (np.ndarray) – flat 1-D array of all polarized fit parameters in the order defined by the destructuring assignment inside this function.

Returns:

structured parameter array of shape (2, 3, 5, n_ansatz, 6) containing [Htlst, Etlst].

Return type:

np.ndarray

gumpgpd.Parameters.ParaManager_Unp(Paralst: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Convert a flat unpolarized parameter list into a structured array.

Most minimizers (e.g. iMinuit) pass parameters as a flat list or tuple. This function reshapes that flat list into a 5-D array of shape (2, 3, 5, n_ansatz, 6) whose axes are:

  • axis 0 – GPD: [H, E]

  • axis 1 – skewness power: [xi^0, xi^2, xi^4]

  • axis 2 – flavor: [u_V, u-bar, d_V, d-bar, g]

  • axis 3 – ansatz index

  • axis 4 – parameters per ansatz: [norm, alpha, beta, alphap, bexp, invm2]

Parameters:

Paralst (np.ndarray) – flat 1-D array of all unpolarized fit parameters in the order defined by the destructuring assignment inside this function.

Returns:

structured parameter array of shape (2, 3, 5, n_ansatz, 6) containing [Hlst, Elst].

Return type:

np.ndarray

gumpgpd.Parameters.beta_loggamma(a: complex, b: complex) → complex[source]

Euler Beta function evaluated via log-gamma for numerical stability.

Computes \(B(a, b) = \Gamma(a)\Gamma(b) / \Gamma(a+b)\) using scipy.special.loggamma to handle complex arguments safely.

Parameters:

  • a (complex) – first argument

  • b (complex) – second argument

Returns:

\(B(a, b)\)

Return type:

complex
